about: EU layer of the NPHI collaboration map: what the European Commission and EU agencies fund or run in health with partner countries. kind 'flagship' = hand-checked Team Europe Initiatives, Global Gateway flagships and HERA/EU4Health actions; kind 'country' = Commission programme-level actions with a health focus, refreshed from IATI by tools/eu_iati.py. EU agency collaborations already in projects.json (ECDC, EMA and Team Europe actions) are shown by the page from that file, not duplicated here. Country names follow the map atlas. amountEURm is the EU or Team Europe amount stated by the source (see summary); null when not stated.

projects.title: Team Europe Initiative: Strengthening Public Health Institutes in Africa
implementers: EU Member State public health institutes
projects.summary: Team Europe and Africa CDC back national public health institutes in Africa: institutional capacity, networking between African and European institutes, workforce training and evidence-based policy advice. A new €50 million Commission programme runs in 10 countries plus a regional strand, implemented by Belgium, France, Germany, Sweden and WHO.
projects.note: Survey cited in the source: European institutes and schools of public health run about 60 projects in 41 African countries, worth about €105 million.

projects.title: AU–EU initiatives on public health institutes, One Health/AMR and digital health
projects.tei: Public Health Institutes; Health Security / One Health; Digital Health
projects.region: Africa (10 AU Member States for NPHIs, 6 for digital health)
projects.summary: Three Global Gateway initiatives launched at the AU in April 2026, led operationally by Africa CDC: support for national public health institutes in 10 countries (surveillance, early warning, response, research, labs), One Health and AMR work with workforce training, and digital health in 6 countries.

projects.title: Establishing Zimbabwe's first National Public Health Institute
projects.summary: Four-year EU grant, implemented with WHO, to set up Zimbabwe's national public health institute with a focus on surveillance, evidence and data-driven policy advice, digital health literacy and NCDs.

projects.title: Team Europe Initiative: Sustainable Health Security through a One Health approach
projects.summary: Team Europe package (over €430 million in total, €145 million from the Commission via EDF, NDICI, HERA/EU4Health and FPI) for health security in Africa: surveillance, labs, AMR and One Health workforce, with Africa CDC as main partner. ECDC's work for Africa CDC sits under this initiative.

projects.title: Team Europe Initiative: Digital Health in Africa
projects.summary: Team Europe support (about €223 million in total, €67 million from the Commission) for interoperable digital health systems and data for preparedness and primary care in Africa.

projects.title: Team Europe Initiative MAV+: manufacturing and access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies in Africa

projects.title: NutriNorte-In Mozambique, where geographical disparities and socio-economic inequalities are increasing, fighting malnutrition ' as both driver and outcome of poverty ' can help tackling extreme poverty and inequality, by investing into the human capital needed to foster inclusive economic growth. Nearly a third of the fast growing Mozambican population is affected by severe food insecurity, while almost 40 percent of children under 5 suffer from chronic malnutrition (stunting), both factors massively hampering the development of the country in human and economic terms. While nutrition remains a priority in the policy agenda of the Government, namely in the 5-year national development plan 2020-2024, national investments (nutrition specific or sensitive are still low. The system struggles to ensure access to key basic social services, often of low quality and marred by high and systemic inequalities, with the northern provinces and the rural areas being the most disadvantaged. Moreover, with now some 31 million habitants and one of the highest fertility rate in the continent, it is expected that the population of Mozambique will reach over 50 million in 2040, thus putting under more pressure basic social and environmental services. This situation is further aggravated by the security crisis in Cabo Delgado and neighbouring provinces, causing massive forced displacement, the impact of recurrent cyclones and climate-related events and the socio-economic consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic. This action builds upon the sound EU experience and lessons learnt from previous investments for improved nutrition under the 10th and 11th European Development Fund (EDF) implemented in several provinces of Mozambique and from emergency nutrition and multisector responses supported by ECHO. While consolidating and building on the work done in Zambezia and Nampula provinces, the Action will expand the EU support for nutrition to Cabo Delgado, where the armed conflict ongoing since 2017 led to a growing humanitarian crisis, with direct negative impact on the nutritional status of communities. The intervention logic closely aligns to the EU multi-sectoral approach to nutrition, and is structured around three strategic components: i)     Nutrition governance; ii)   Scale up of key nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive actions, with a focus on the effective delivery of quality key nutrition, health and WASH services at community level; iii)  Knowledge-building and advocacy, including civil society engagement. The Action will be implemented in the three provinces of Zambezia, Nampula and Cabo Delgado, while advocacy activities carried out by civil society will have a national coverage. It will have a duration of 60 months, with an EU contribution of EUR 30 million.
